model: claude-code (interactive; 8 strict + 5 soft-gate per-category Layer-2 agents). tag.py not built.
phase: Phase 1 (Layer 2 tagging) — strict core + soft-gate extended pass, 2026-06-01 run. Stored for on-demand Phase 2 retrieval; no target category yet.

tiers.core: Strict forward-looking gate: names a new container/behavior/aesthetic/mode. The high-signal pool for Phase 2 generation.
tiers.extended: Soft breadth gate: culturally legible but often descriptive. Kept to enrich the corpus and evolve the framework over time. forward_looking flag distinguishes the genuinely-novel extended items from descriptive recoveries.

notes: 209 of 214 harvested signals kept (89 core + 120 extended); only 5 true non-signals dropped (tweet-aggregation, a pure cinematography how-to, an open-call page, an event guide, an exhibition announcement).
Filter for the strict forward-looking core with tier=='core', or for everything genuinely novel with forward_looking==true (regardless of tier). 134 of 209 kept are forward_looking==true.
Pools place a signal in a single substrate only if high/medium confidence; unsettled OR low-confidence feed the unsettled pool (per v1.1 spec). The unsettled pool is intentionally the largest.
Use fetch.py to query this corpus by --substrate / --category / --tier / --forward-looking / --source / --confidence when a target category arrives.

signals.title: Roda Medhat Subverts Traditional Kurdish Narratives Into Modern Tactile Experiences
signals.summary: Profile of Toronto-based Kurdish artist Roda Medhat, who pushes traditional West Asian textiles into sculpture, reworking Kurdish narratives into tactile contemporary forms.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Status (heritage/distinction) and Agency (reworking inherited narrative), but the core move is binding a diasporic community to its narrative through tactile form — recognition and belonging via material memory.
signals.novelty_note: Refuses textile-as-flat-craft, converting woven cultural narrative into three-dimensional sculpture so heritage becomes something you move around rather than read.

signals.title: Wander through Adrienna Matzeg's Embroidered, Late-Night City Explorations
signals.summary: Profile of textile artist Adrienna Matzeg, whose embroidered works render late-night storefronts and cityscapes from her travels through Asian cities.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Vitality (urban aliveness) and Connection (witnessing place); the slow, consoling labor of embroidering transient night-scenes pulls toward Coping but doesn't fully resolve — feeds the unsettled pool.
signals.novelty_note: Refuses photography as the medium for the fleeting urban night, slowing an instant of transient city-glow into months of stitch.

signals.title: This Risograph Studio Celebrates 400 Artist Postcards Mailed Around the Globe
signals.summary: Feature on Gabriella Marcella's Risotto risograph studio, marking 400 artist-designed postcards mailed worldwide as a collaborative print project.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Light Status pull (artist-network in-group) but dominated by Connection: a distributed mail-art ritual that binds a global community of makers through physical exchange.
signals.novelty_note: Refuses the screen as the channel for networked artist exchange, reviving slow physical mail-art as the binding infrastructure of a global creative community.

signals.title: Nuart Aberdeen 2026: Poetry In The Streets
signals.summary: Feature on Nuart Aberdeen 2026, billed as the first street-art festival centered on poetry and text-based work, with artists including Robert Montgomery, Remi Rough, and Molly Hankinson.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Pulls across Connection (public address), Vitality (street energy), and Agency (text as voice in shared space); a new festival container reorienting street art from image to language doesn't yet resolve to one need.
signals.novelty_note: Refuses the image-first convention of street art, making poetry/text the organizing principle of a public festival — a new container for street art as language.

signals.title: Artist Lee Ufan, Who Turns 90 Next Month, Will Change How You Feel About Time
signals.summary: Interview with Mono-ha artist Lee Ufan ahead of his 90th birthday, on the spare paintings and stone-and-steel sculptures (Naoshima, Venice) that slow time and heighten bodily awareness.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Coping (slowing time as consolation against overwhelm); chosen Vitality because the named effect is heightened bodily awareness and felt presence — aliveness through reduction.
signals.novelty_note: Names a new mode of evaluating art by the bodily time-perception it induces rather than by image or object — slowness as the deliverable.

signals.title: For Artist Cecilia Vicuña, Being Busy Is Not a Sign of Success
signals.summary: Profile of 77-year-old Chilean-born artist-poet Cecilia Vicuña during a banner year, on her quipu-influenced sculpture, poetry, and resistance to productivity-as-success.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Status (redefining what success looks like) and Coping (refusal of overwhelm); chosen Agency because the core is self-authorship and refusal of the productivity regime.
signals.novelty_note: Names a new mode of evaluating an artistic life by refusing busyness-as-success — anti-productivity as the measure of a practice.

signals.title: Artist Martine Gutierrez on Staging the Most Provocative Performance of Her Career
signals.summary: Profile/interview with artist Martine Gutierrez on a lottery-based performance work at Ryan Lee Gallery, framed as the most provocative of her career.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Pulls across Status (who is selected/valued), Agency (ceding authorial control to chance), and Vitality (charged live event); a lottery as the structural form of the work doesn't resolve to one need.
signals.novelty_note: Refuses curatorial/authorial selection by making a lottery the structural mechanism of the artwork — chance as the ritual form.

signals.title: The Artists of 'Greater New York' Give the City's Art Scene a Temp Check
signals.summary: Feature gathering 22 artists from MoMA PS1's quinquennial 'Greater New York' on the economic realities of making art in the city in 2026.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Status (location in the art economy) and Connection (collective scene witnessing); chosen Coping as it surfaces a collective managing of economic weight, but the polyphonic temp-check form keeps it loosely held.
signals.novelty_note: Refuses the single-artist profile, using a 22-voice collective temp-check as a new form for taking the emotional/economic pulse of a scene.

signals.title: Artistic Noise: In Conversation with Calder Zwicky
signals.summary: Interview with Calder Zwicky about Artistic Noise, a program engaging young people through art-making and youth-driven creative practice.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Agency (youth voice/self-authorship); chosen Connection because the structure is a community program binding young people through shared making and recognition.
signals.novelty_note: Frames youth art-making as community infrastructure rather than instruction — art as a binding social program, not a skill transfer.

signals.title: Maia Chao: 'BEING MOVED' at the Whitney
signals.summary: Review of Maia Chao's 'BEING MOVED' at the Whitney, examining the project's engagement with audience, movement, and institutional space.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Pulls across Connection (audience participation), Agency (who gets to move/act in the institution), and Vitality (felt movement); a participatory restructuring of the museum relation doesn't resolve to one need.
signals.novelty_note: Refuses passive spectatorship, restructuring the museum encounter around audience movement and emotional displacement as the medium.

signals.title: In Conversation with Iréne Norén (Reclaiming the Sacred)
signals.summary: Interview with artist Iréne Norén on reclaiming the sacred in her practice.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Connection (ritual/binding) and Vitality (felt intensity); chosen Coping loosely as reclaiming the sacred is a search for refuge/meaning, but the thin summary and cross-cutting sacred frame keep confidence low.
signals.novelty_note: Refuses secular-only contemporary art framing, proposing the sacred as a usable register for present-day practice.

signals.title: What Artists Build for One Another: Notes from Wassaic
signals.summary: Essay from the Wassaic Project on artist communities and the infrastructures of mutual support artists build for each other.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Light Agency pull (artists self-organizing); dominated by Connection — the explicit subject is mutual-support infrastructure and community binding among artists.
signals.novelty_note: Refuses the lone-genius and market frame, naming the mutual-aid infrastructure artists build for each other as the actual subject of an art community.

signals.title: A Low-Volume Declaration: Becoming Cyborg as Ethics
signals.summary: Essay framing 'becoming cyborg' as an ethical stance, reading body-technology hybridity through a low-volume, declarative register.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Pulls across Agency (self-authorship via tech), Vitality (altered embodiment), and Coping (living with technological condition); body-tech hybridity as ethics is pre-categorical, hence unsettled.
signals.novelty_note: Refuses the loud transhumanist register, proposing 'becoming cyborg' as a quiet ethical stance rather than spectacle or upgrade.

signals.title: Felix Beaudry: Soft Bodies, Hard Tech
signals.summary: Interview with artist Felix Beaudry on the tension between soft, textile/bodily materials and hard technology in his work.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Pulls across Vitality (bodily/material intensity) and Agency (mastery over material-tech tension); the soft-body/hard-tech boundary is the cross-cutting subject, so unsettled.
signals.novelty_note: Refuses the clean digital-fabrication aesthetic, staging textile softness against hard technology as the work's unresolved core.

signals.title: Driver of Speculation: In Conversation with Alice Bucknell
signals.summary: Interview with artist Alice Bucknell on speculative fiction, game engines, and ecological worldbuilding in her video/installation work.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Pulls across Agency (worldbuilding/authorship), Coping (rehearsing ecological futures), and Vitality (immersive intensity); game-engine speculative ecology is genuinely cross-cutting.
signals.novelty_note: Refuses documentary or didactic eco-art, using game engines to make speculative, playable ecological futures as the form of environmental thinking.

signals.title: Beyond Cell Doors: Russell Craig's Vision
signals.summary: Profile/interview with formerly incarcerated artist Russell Craig on making work that addresses imprisonment and the carceral system.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Coping (processing incarceration) and Connection (witnessing carceral experience); chosen Agency because the core is reclaiming voice and self-authorship after the carceral erasure of it.
signals.novelty_note: Refuses the outside-observer carceral-art frame, centering the formerly incarcerated maker's own authorship as the structural shift.

signals.title: Why We Should Be Having More Platonic Sleepovers
signals.summary: Essay arguing for the revival of non-romantic adult sleepovers as a way to deepen platonic intimacy and counter the touch-starved isolation of contemporary friendship.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Coping (counter to isolation/touch-starvation) but the dominant move is proposing a new binding ritual for adult platonic intimacy, which is squarely Connection.
signals.novelty_note: Proposes a revived adult ritual container — the platonic sleepover — as deliberate infrastructure for non-romantic physical intimacy.

signals.title: The Summer of the Jelly: What Our Obsession with Transparency Really Reveals
signals.summary: Trend essay using the season's jelly/transparent aesthetic in fashion and design as a lens onto cultural desires around visibility, surface, and concealment.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names an emerging aesthetic (jelly/transparency) and a new mode of reading it — visibility/concealment — cutting across Status (taste-coding), Vitality (sensual surface) and Coping (anxiety about exposure) without resolving. Pre-categorical, so unsettled.
signals.novelty_note: Frames transparency-as-material not as taste but as a collective stance toward being seen/hidden — a fresh evaluative lens on a just-emerging aesthetic.

signals.title: The Female Artists Turning Internet Slop into Fine Art
signals.summary: Interview-led feature on women artists who repurpose AI-generated 'slop' and digital detritus into fine art, reclaiming devalued internet imagery as material.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Vitality (material intensity) and Status (reclassifying devalued imagery as fine art), but the dominant gesture is reclamation/authorship — taking AI detritus and asserting voice over it.
signals.novelty_note: An emerging practice of treating AI 'slop' as raw material to be authored against, inverting who controls value in machine-generated imagery.

signals.title: Caroline Wong on 'Girls Who Devour', Women Eating in the Age of GLP-1s and #Girlhood
signals.summary: Interview with Caroline Wong on her 'Girls Who Devour' project, exploring women's relationship to appetite and eating amid the rise of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs and online girlhood discourse.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Agency (reclaiming appetite as self-authorship) and Coping (body anxiety in the GLP-1 era), but the central image — women devouring, appetite as force — reads as Vitality: bodily hunger asserted against a culture of suppression.
signals.novelty_note: Stakes appetite-as-vitality explicitly against the GLP-1 moment, naming a new tension between pharmaceutical hunger-suppression and the celebration of female bodily wanting.

signals.title: Adjust, Comply, Recalculate
signals.summary: Renee Robinson essay examining how desire for luxury and quality goods becomes entangled with consumer debt and predatory lending, framing acquisition as a cycle of financial obligation.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Coping (managing financial weight/obligation) but the engine is status acquisition — naming the debt-treadmill that underwrites luxury signaling.
signals.novelty_note: Reframes luxury acquisition not as signaling but as an ongoing financial-obligation cycle — desire metered through predatory lending as the hidden structure of taste.

signals.title: College for Creative Studies BA 2026: Cultural Histories
signals.summary: Graduate-show feature on the Detroit institution's 2026 BA class, profiling emerging designers who mine cultural and historical narratives in their collections.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Graduate work, forward-looking by definition. The cohort mines cultural/historical narrative — touches Connection (heritage) and Status (taste formation) but is too diffuse across a class to resolve to one need.
signals.novelty_note: Emerging-designer cohort treating cultural history as the primary design generator rather than form/silhouette — a leading indicator of narrative-over-aesthetic pedagogy.

signals.title: Accademia Costume & Moda BA 2026: Memory and Material
signals.summary: Coverage of Rome's Accademia Costume & Moda 2026 BA graduates, whose collections interrogate material heritage and personal memory through construction.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Graduate work, forward-looking by definition. Personal memory + material heritage leans Coping (narrative/consolation through material) but also Connection (heritage). Low confidence; feeds unsettled pool.
signals.novelty_note: Emerging cohort using garment construction as a memory-and-grief vehicle — personal memory encoded structurally rather than depicted.

signals.title: Who Gets the Credit?
signals.summary: Essay on the overlooked legal frameworks governing creative attribution in fashion, arguing the industry systematically ignores who deserves authorship credit.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Status (credit as hierarchy/recognition) but the core move is authorship and the right to claim one's labor — voice against systemic erasure.
signals.novelty_note: Names a new mode of evaluating fashion by authorship-attribution and legal credit rather than by the named house — surfacing invisible creative labor as the unit of value.

signals.title: Oliver Jeanes, the Designer Mining the Pleasures of Bad Taste
signals.summary: AnOther Name to Know profile of emerging Central Saint Martins designer Oliver Jeanes, who builds collections around freestyle disco dancing and the deliberate pleasures of 'bad taste.'
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Obvious Status pull (bad taste is a taste-coding inversion), but the generative source is bodily — freestyle disco dancing, pleasure, movement. Vitality, with Status as the secondary register being subverted.
signals.novelty_note: Builds collections from freestyle dance as the design method and embraces 'bad taste' as a positive value — a new evaluative mode where kinetic pleasure trumps refinement.

signals.title: On Fashioning the Body: Karoline Vitto and Sinéad O'Dwyer in Conversation
signals.summary: In Conversation between designers Karoline Vitto and Sinéad O'Dwyer on body-inclusive design and embodiment, occasioned by the Met Costume Institute.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Connection (recognition/belonging for non-normative bodies) and Agency (self-authorship of the body), but the dominant move is designing from and for embodiment — the fleshly body as the design premise.
signals.novelty_note: Treats the unidealized body's actual flesh as the structural starting point for garment design rather than something to be concealed or corrected.

signals.title: Groundwork
signals.summary: Profile of London design group Resolve Collective (Akil and Seth Scafe-Smith, Melissa Haniff), tracing its Brixton activist origins and projects redistributing reclaimed materials from institutions like the Barbican and Tate Liverpool to grassroots groups.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Connection (grassroots community-building) strongly, but the structural move is material redistribution as a power-redirecting act — re-routing institutional resources to grassroots groups.
signals.novelty_note: A design practice whose primary output is the redistribution of reclaimed institutional material to grassroots groups — design-as-logistics-of-redistribution rather than object-making.

signals.title: Patta Selects: Daniel Smedeman
signals.summary: Interview with Amsterdam nail artist and Glazed Salon co-founder Daniel Smedeman on nail design as a discipline, his fashion-house collaborations, and his book project 'Unguis Oracle.'
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Status (taste/craft distinction) and Agency (elevating a marginal craft to discipline); the elevation of nail art to a serious medium sits unresolved between bodily ornament/pleasure and craft-mastery — leans Vitality, low confidence.
signals.novelty_note: Frames nail art as a standalone discipline with its own canon ('Unguis Oracle'), a new mode of taking a peripheral beauty craft seriously as authored practice.

signals.title: Rumor and the Architecture of the Guestlist
signals.summary: Profile of Rumor, an event-software platform that reframes the guestlist as cultural infrastructure rather than logistics, arguing that curating who is in the room (vs. ticketing) is what makes a gathering's energy compound. Frames exclusive access itself as a source of brand legitimacy across Fashion Week, Art Basel and Coachella.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Connection (the energy of a room, who is co-present) but resolves to Status: location in social space, in-group codes, access-as-legitimacy. Connection is the cover story; distinction is the mechanism.
signals.novelty_note: Treats the guestlist as a productized layer of cultural infrastructure — access-curation as a SaaS category and a measurable source of brand legitimacy, not mere event logistics.

signals.title: Oddbird and the Architecture of Absence
signals.summary: Profile/criticism using non-alcoholic wine brand Oddbird as a lens on shifting attitudes toward drinking, arguing the category is now built intentionally from the ground up rather than as a deficient substitute. Positions the choice as participation in ritual rather than acceptance of absence.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Cross-cuts Agency (sober autonomy, refusal), Connection (staying in the ritual), and Status (NA-as-affirmative-taste rather than abstinence-as-lack). Resolves toward Status because the new move is reframing the choice as a positive taste signal.
signals.novelty_note: Names a new mode of evaluation: a category designed 'from the ground up' as presence rather than substitute — absence reframed as an affirmative ritual choice.

signals.title: TASTESLOP
signals.summary: Emily Segal/Martti Kalliala coin 'tasteslop' for aesthetically refined signals stripped of social context and authenticity, produced when AI or generic curation extracts taste markers without understanding their meaning. Argues genuine taste requires social validation and esoteric knowledge AI cannot replicate, and that tech's obsession with taste is anxiety about whether economic capital can capture cultural capital.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Coins a new evaluative concept; primary fit Status (taste, distinction, cultural-vs-economic capital, esoteric in-group knowledge as the thing AI can't fake). Brushes the AI/unsettled cluster but the analysis is explicitly about hierarchy and signaling.
signals.novelty_note: Coins 'tasteslop' — a named failure mode of AI/generic curation that reproduces taste markers without the social context that gives them value; reframes taste as the last moat against capital capturing cultural capital.

signals.title: Inside and outside
signals.summary: Paula Mejía essay on the design of security envelopes — the patterned interiors of mailed envelopes — as an overlooked piece of everyday visual culture and a meditation on privacy, concealment and the aesthetics of the mundane.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names a new evaluative lens (aesthetics-of-concealment / privacy-as-design applied to the most overlooked everyday object). Touches Coping (concealment as protection) and faintly Status (connoisseurship of the mundane) but resolves to neither — pre-categorical.
signals.novelty_note: Elevates security-envelope patterning into a named object of design attention — concealment-as-aesthetic, treating privacy infrastructure as a legible visual genre.

signals.title: Panic! At the post-reality (Katherine Williams on How to See Like a Machine)
signals.summary: Katherine Williams reviews Trevor Paglen's 'How to See Like a Machine: Images After AI,' arguing the more interesting move isn't fortifying defenses against deepfakes but recognizing democracy itself as a kind of deepfake. Engages computer vision and generative AI as forces reshaping how reality is perceived and trusted.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Cross-cuts Coping (managing post-truth overwhelm) and Agency (how one orients when verification collapses), but its central move — reframing 'reality vs deepfake' as a category that no longer holds — is genuinely pre-categorical.
signals.novelty_note: Names a new way of relating to images: stop defending against deepfakes and instead treat reality/democracy as themselves machine-mediated constructions.

signals.title: Everything's probably fake now
signals.summary: Ryan Broderick argues social feeds are now dominated by low-paid Global South 'clippers' who reshare content for AI firms and marketers, making original content economically unviable. Cites a Rwandan creator (@whotfisrw) and the stark math — ~$1M/month buys 600M views across 35,000 videos vs. a UK journalist earning £140 for 1.5M TikTok views.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Identifies a new structural form — the 'clipper' economy as an emergent labor/distribution layer of the feed. Touches Status (collapsing value of authorship) and Agency (creators displaced from voice) but is too new and cross-cutting to settle.
signals.novelty_note: Surfaces the 'clipper' supply chain as a named emergent structure: a Global-South reshare labor economy that makes original content economically unviable and severs views from authorship.

signals.title: An internet after search engines
signals.summary: Broderick essay on what online consumer culture looks like as traditional search engines decline and AI answer-engines and social discovery displace Google as the front door to the web. (Body not fully retrievable via fetch; title/date/author verified from archive.)
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Describes a new structural form — the post-search 'front door' (answer-engines + social discovery) — reorganizing how consumers find everything online. Brushes Agency (navigation/choice without search) but is fundamentally an emergent, undecided reconfiguration of the discovery layer.
signals.novelty_note: Names the emergence of a post-search-engine discovery regime — AI answer-engines and social feeds replacing the Google query as the structural front door to consumer culture.

signals.title: 'Yesteryear' Author Caro Claire Burke on Her Bestselling Tradwife Novel
signals.summary: Author interview tied to a screen adaptation, unpacking the cultural fascination with the 'tradwife' phenomenon and how the novel interrogates nostalgia and gendered domesticity.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Tradwife is fundamentally a status/distinction code, but the novel's interrogation pulls toward Coping (nostalgia as refuge) and Connection (idealized domestic belonging). The new container is the trend crossing into prestige fiction/screen adaptation.
signals.novelty_note: Tradwife migrating from social-media aesthetic into literary fiction and prestige screen adaptation — the trend acquiring a self-interrogating narrative container.

signals.title: The internet's favorite horror subgenre is breaking into the big time
signals.summary: Analysis of how liminal horror (Backrooms, dreamcore, dream pools) moved from internet niche to mainstream cinema, arguing its appeal lies in post-pandemic nostalgia and a deliberate handmade, anti-AI aesthetic that audiences read as authentically human.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary Coping: liminal horror processes post-pandemic dislocation and the uncanny weightlessness of empty space. Touches Vitality (the bodily prickle of dread) and unsettled (the anti-AI 'authentically human' read is a brand-new evaluative axis).
signals.novelty_note: An internet-native subgenre breaking into mainstream cinema PLUS a new evaluative axis: 'handmade = authentically human = valuable' as explicit anti-AI audience criterion.

signals.title: Meme Culture's Corrosive Effect on the American Heart
signals.summary: Alyssa Charpentier argues memes function as thought-terminating clichés that dehumanize people across the political spectrum, warning that celebrating tragedy through humor echoes historical patterns of dehumanization preceding authoritarianism.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names a new evaluative frame: memes-as-thought-terminating-cliché. Touches Connection (in-group binding via shared joke), Status (meme fluency as code), and Coping (humor as distraction) without resolving — the claim is precisely that these functions have a corrosive cost.
signals.novelty_note: Reframes the meme not as content but as an emotional-cognitive technology with a measurable dehumanizing effect — a new evaluative frame for the culture's default humor form.

signals.title: Why Tokyo Has So Many Record Stores
signals.summary: Essay examining how Tokyo sustains roughly 250 record stores while Western cities lost theirs, attributing survival to aggressive store differentiation, rail-driven walkable neighborhoods, and a collector culture treating physical media as cultural objects.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary Status: physical-media collecting as taste, distinction, and curatorial signaling in an era of infinite streaming. Touches Connection (store as third place) and Coping (the tangible object as refuge from the feed).
signals.novelty_note: Posits a replicable structural model (hyper-differentiation + walkable density + object-reverence) for how physical-media retail can survive streaming, not just nostalgia for it.

signals.title: 'Recomposed' Performs a Fundamental Interpretation of the Music Industry
signals.summary: Books essay on Kyle Devine's work, reframing the music industry through an ecological lens that foregrounds the material and environmental costs of recorded-music formats.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names a new evaluative frame: judging music by its material/environmental cost rather than sound or culture. Cross-cuts Status (eco-conscious distinction), Coping (ecological guilt), and Agency (ethical refusal of formats) without settling.
signals.novelty_note: An ecological/material-cost frame for evaluating music consumption — shifting the locus of value from the song to its physical-format footprint.

signals.title: Kim Petras Takes A Detour Off The Pop Highway
signals.summary: Interview/feature on Kim Petras pivoting away from mainstream pop conventions, examining the artistic and commercial stakes of her stylistic detour.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary Agency: deliberate refusal of the optimized mainstream-pop pipeline as self-authorship. Touches Vitality (artistic aliveness vs formula) and Status (prestige of the 'brave detour'). Kept as a structural-shift signal, not a biography.
signals.novelty_note: Frames a deliberate exit from the streaming-optimized pop pipeline as a positive artistic move, signaling an emerging anti-optimization stance among mainstream pop artists.

signals.title: Low Culture Essay: Mary Chiney on Stanley Okorie's Nollywood Soundtracks
signals.summary: Essay arguing early Nollywood's true avant-garde lived in its soundtracks, with composer Stanley Okorie writing hyper-specific synth-pop that narrated film plots; Chiney warns that streaming algorithms demanding 'chill vibes' from African music threaten these works' survival.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Forward-looking structural claim: streaming's 'chill vibes' demand actively flattens and endangers a hyper-specific musical form — algorithm-as-aesthetic-gatekeeper. Cross-cuts Status (canonizing an overlooked avant-garde), Agency (resistance to flattening), and Coping (archive as survival).
signals.novelty_note: Articulates how streaming-platform mood-categorization ('chill vibes') operates as a homogenizing force that can extinguish a non-Western musical idiom — algorithm as active aesthetic editor.

signals.title: Rotting Tape and the Gentrification of African Pop: Why We Must Save the Nollywood Archive
signals.summary: Black Sky Thinking essay on the physical decay of Nollywood film and music archives, framing preservation as a fight against the gentrification and Western repackaging of African pop heritage.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary Agency: preservation-as-resistance, asserting control over whose heritage survives and on whose terms. Touches Status (canon-formation) and Connection (binding a diaspora to its past). Borders on advocacy essay, so low confidence.
signals.novelty_note: Frames archival preservation as anti-gentrification activism — naming Western repackaging of African pop as a form of cultural displacement to be resisted.

signals.title: Cannes Tried to Ban Nudity. Celebrities Revolted—and an Iconic Fashion Tradition Was Born.
signals.summary: Fashion-culture feature on Cannes 2026's nudity ban and the celebrity pushback, tracing how red-carpet defiance crystallized into an enduring festival fashion tradition.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary Agency: bodily refusal of an institutional dress code as a public act of defiance. Touches Status (red-carpet distinction) and Vitality (the exposed body as force). Kept because the piece claims a new ritual form crystallized — defiance-as-tradition.
signals.novelty_note: A new ritual container: institutional prohibition generating its own counter-tradition of codified red-carpet defiance — the ban itself becoming the engine of a recurring fashion form.

signals.title: He Was Supposed to Be "Canceled." He Just Broke One of Michael Jackson's Most Enduring Records.
signals.summary: Music-culture essay on Drake's chart resurgence post-Kendrick feud, interrogating what 'cancellation' means commercially when an artist still breaks Michael Jackson's Billboard records.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names a new evaluative frame: the decoupling of moral 'cancellation' from commercial performance. Cross-cuts Status (reputation/hierarchy) and Agency (the public's supposed power to punish, shown impotent) without resolving — the metric of consequence itself is in question.
signals.novelty_note: Surfaces the collapse of 'cancellation' as a meaningful predictor of commercial fate — a new frame in which moral consensus and market power have visibly come apart.

signals.title: field notes from a phone-free future
signals.summary: Aleksic reports on an emerging countercultural movement rejecting smartphone dependency and algorithmic optimization in favor of unmediated, subjective experience. Frames it as 'representation against representation' - a refusal to let corporate platforms categorize and commodify lived experience.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary Agency: refusal and self-authorship — reclaiming experience from algorithmic capture. Touches Vitality (unmediated lived intensity) and Coping (relief from optimization overwhelm), but the oppositional 'representation against representation' framing makes refusal load-bearing.
signals.novelty_note: New evaluative frame: phone-refusal recast not as digital-detox self-care but as a political-aesthetic act of withholding oneself from platform legibility.

signals.title: the monsters hiding in your algorithm
signals.summary: Argues that beneath TikTok's curated algorithmic surface lies an incomprehensible 'terra incognita' of absurdist, nonsensical content. Positions these online 'monsters' as modern mythology - warnings about the unknowable vastness beneath our ordered digital world, like ancient mythical creatures explaining the inexplicable.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Genuinely pre-categorical. Touches Coping (mythology as a device for metabolizing the incomprehensible) and Vitality (lure of the absurd/uncanny), but the signal is about the culture not yet having a frame for the algorithmic unknown itself.
signals.novelty_note: Treats algorithmic feeds as having an unmappable interior, importing the 'here be monsters' cartographic-mythology frame to platform structure.

signals.title: you don't know where anything comes from
signals.summary: Contends that consumers are willfully ignorant of the origins of products, ideas, and memes they consume, making them 'civically negligent' and diminishing lived experience. Argues that actively questioning sources - of wool sweaters, avocados, or viral memes alike - is what yields genuine satisfaction and better citizenship.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary Agency: source-tracing as an active, self-authoring discipline restoring mastery over one's consumption. Touches Status (provenance-literacy as distinction) and Coping (the 'genuine satisfaction' payoff).
signals.novelty_note: Collapses material supply-chain provenance and meme/idea provenance into a single civic-virtue obligation — 'origin-literacy' across objects and information alike.

signals.title: moloch and the machines
signals.summary: Frames modern society as Moloch, sacrificing human connection for algorithmic optimization, and proposes real-world community events as the antidote - demonstrated via a public reading of Ginsberg's 'Howl' in Washington Square Park. Explores the paradox of using social media to critique social media, concluding 'the event is the medium.'
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary Connection: the prescribed antidote is the IRL binding ritual / co-presence event that resists algorithmic atomization. Touches Agency (refusal of optimization) and Coping (relief from Moloch-overwhelm), but 'the event is the medium' makes communal gathering load-bearing.
signals.novelty_note: Inverts McLuhan into 'the event is the medium' — the in-person gathering itself, not its content or documentation, positioned as the message and the cure.

signals.title: how to look at brainrot
signals.summary: Argues that AI-generated 'brainrot' memes deserve serious artistic consideration as contemporary folk art with genuine emotional and psychological effects. Advocates analyzing memes through phenomenology and context rather than dismissing them, since they 'resonate with other human beings.'
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Cross-cutting and pre-categorical. Touches Vitality (affective jolt brainrot delivers), Connection ('resonate with other human beings'), and Status (taste-move of taking low content seriously), but the culture hasn't decided what need AI-folk-art serves.
signals.novelty_note: A phenomenological-folk-art criticism applied to AI-generated brainrot, asserting machine-made disposable content can carry genuine aesthetic and emotional weight.

signals.title: symbiotic virality
signals.summary: Distinguishes 'parasitic virality' (one-sided extraction treating people as means) from 'mutualistic virality' (mutual benefit), arguing that social media virality often exploits people. Contends meaningful online communication requires prioritizing community-building over content creation for its own sake.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Leans Connection (mutual benefit / community over content), but the real contribution is a new biological taxonomy of virality-as-relationship-type spanning Status (reach) and Agency (refusing extractive use). Too new a frame to settle.
signals.novelty_note: Imports an ecology/symbiosis taxonomy (parasitic vs mutualistic) to classify virality as a relationship type rather than a metric.

signals.title: 'The Drama' and the microgenerational digital divide
signals.summary: Uses the film 'The Drama' to argue the Zoomer-Millennial divide hinges on whether one's adolescent transgressions were digitally documented. Millennials' youthful mistakes went unrecorded, while Zoomers face permanently archived pasts, producing divergent attitudes toward guilt, accountability, and forgiveness.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary Coping: the felt weight is the permanently archived self and the guilt of an un-erasable past. Touches Status (generational in-group identity) and Connection (forgiveness as relational), but living-with-the-archive is the core need.
signals.novelty_note: Defines a micro-generational boundary not by birth year but by whether one's adolescent transgressions were digitally recorded — documentation status as the new cohort marker.

signals.title: People prefer A.I. art because people prefer bad art
signals.summary: Argues people favor AI-generated art not for superior creativity but because they prefer accessible, straightforward kitsch over challenging human work. Critiques Scott Alexander's AI Art Turing Test as designed to obscure distinguishing features, citing a Nature study where AI poems outscored Eliot and Shakespeare for being more 'straightforward.'
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary Status: a taste/distinction claim — preference for accessible kitsch over difficult human work as a marker of where one sits aesthetically. Touches Coping (comfort of the 'straightforward') and unsettled (what AI-art preference reveals is still being argued).
signals.novelty_note: Reframes the AI-art debate from 'can machines be creative' to a status/taste claim — preference for AI reveals an appetite for legible kitsch over difficulty.

signals.title: Sexless Little Carnivores
signals.summary: Emily Kenway traces the cultural history of pet food, from Victorian fears that fresh meat caused canine 'nymphomania' to today's premium 'ancestral'-diet brands. Argues these brands sell the fantasy of a pet's wildness while delivering fully domesticated predators eating from pouches, a proxy for evolving human-animal control.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names a new mode of evaluating consumption: the 'ancestral'/wildness fantasy projected onto a domesticated body. Touches Status (premium-brand ancestral-diet signaling) and Coping (managing the dissonance of control via fantasy). Reads near-unsettled.
signals.novelty_note: The commodification of vicarious wildness — buying back an animal's (and by proxy one's own) suppressed predatory vitality through premium product, while the actual body stays fully managed.

signals.title: Eight People, One Hob
signals.summary: Nell Whittaker critiques the social-media romanticization of communal house-share cooking, arguing shared kitchens usually stem from financial necessity, not commune ideology. Includes a practical 'recipe' for cooking five distinct meals on a single stovetop as a portrait of the unaesthetic mundanity of cohabitation.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary Connection: the constrained, unromantic binding ritual of sharing one stovetop. Touches Coping (managing economic precarity through shared infrastructure) and Status (the taste-economy of romanticized house-share content).
signals.novelty_note: An emerging anti-aesthetic of constraint-cooking — the choreography of many bodies negotiating one stove as a felt form of belonging-under-pressure, explicitly de-romanticized.

signals.title: Your Machine is Killing You
signals.summary: Fenja Akinde-Hummel explores microwave conspiracy theories and the domestic anxieties around appliance technology, particularly as they circulate within families. Treats kitchen-tech fear as a window onto distrust of modernity and the gendered politics of the home.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary Coping: kitchen-tech fear as a container for diffuse mortality/contamination anxiety, transmitted along family lines. Touches Connection (the family as circulatory system for these fears) and unsettled (pre-categorical body-tech-home dread).
signals.novelty_note: The kitchen appliance as a site of bodily contamination panic and a named emerging anxiety about the home turning against the body, circulating as inherited family lore.

signals.title: The Internet is Air with Maya Man
signals.summary: Em Mai Chmiel interviews artist Maya Man on internet culture, self-curation as embodied performance, and her skepticism toward fashionable neo-Luddism. Draws on Man's background as a competition dancer and her StarQuest/StarPower project staging the aestheticized self, ahead of her bitforms solo show opening March 19, 2026.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names a new way of relating: self-curation as embodied performance with the internet as ambient medium ('air') rather than a tool to refuse. Cross-cuts Vitality (the performed live body), Status (self-curation as distinction) and Agency (self-authorship through staging).
signals.novelty_note: Rejecting neo-Luddism in favor of the internet as inescapable atmosphere, with the curated body as continuous live performance — a post-refusal stance toward embodiment online.

signals.title: The Last Cow
signals.summary: Sarah Thankam Mathews contributes a dystopian fiction piece on longing for something one has never had, using scarcity of dairy/sweetness as its central image. Treats the cultural and bodily weight of craving in a depleted future. (NOTE: cakezine.org domain is compromised; editorial now lives at cakezine.substack.com.)
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Fiction with a cultural-framing payload — names an emerging anxiety (climate/scarcity grief expressed through appetite for what is gone). Primary Coping (felt weight of anticipatory loss); touches Vitality (appetite/sweetness as aliveness). Low confidence (single fiction piece).
signals.novelty_note: Names a forward anxiety of inherited scarcity — longing for a bodily pleasure (sweetness) one has never tasted, as the affective signature of a depleted future.

signals.title: Was It Worth It?
signals.summary: Adam Dalva connects Ozempic, grief, and the 'theater of all-you-can-eat dining,' interrogating appetite, indulgence, and the body in an era of pharmaceutical hunger-suppression. Sweetness and excess become a lens on contemporary anxieties about desire.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary Vitality — appetite, desire, indulgence as felt aliveness, now pharmaceutically dampened. Strongly touches Coping (grief, managing desire's suppression) such that it nearly reads unsettled. Held in Vitality because the central object is appetite-as-life-force being chemically altered.
signals.novelty_note: 'All-you-can-eat as theater' and the post-Ozempic re-evaluation of indulgence — appetite reframed as a question ('was it worth it?') rather than a given, naming the felt loss of desire itself.

signals.title: What A Mess
signals.summary: A conversation with chef Brooks Headley on running a lacto-vegetarian restaurant (Superiority Burger) in carnivorous NYC, treating dessert and meatless cooking as cultural provocation. Frames the restaurant as a ritual space negotiating pleasure and ethics.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Frames the restaurant as a ritual space negotiating pleasure and ethics. Primary Vitality (dessert/sensual indulgence held against ethical restraint). Touches Status (meatless as in-group provocation) and Agency (refusal of the meat default). Low confidence — single restaurant profile.
signals.novelty_note: Dessert and meatlessness positioned as pleasure-forward provocation rather than ascetic sacrifice — pleasure as the carrier of an ethical refusal.

signals.title: Notes Towards Biotic Architecture (We the Bacteria)
signals.summary: A Beatriz Colomina and Mark Wigley piece (with Josh Daube) on biotic, microbial framings of architecture, reconceiving buildings and bodies as colonized by and continuous with bacterial life. Pushes design discourse toward the entanglement of the built environment and the body's biome.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names a genuinely new way of relating body, home and life — building and biome as continuous, the self as microbial colony. Cross-cuts Vitality (body as teeming system), Connection (continuity with non-human life) and Coping (dissolving the body's boundary). Pre-categorical.
signals.novelty_note: A biotic design paradigm that erases the boundary between built environment and the body's biome — the home as a living organism continuous with the inhabitant's flesh.

signals.title: Into the Right-Wing Dreamworld
signals.summary: Mitch Therieau argues the second Trump administration governs through propagandistic imagery rather than rhetoric, fusing fascist iconography, frontier mythology, and state violence into emotionally resonant 'dream logic' symbols (e.g. a viral penguin video). The visual regime expresses an annihilationist impulse: a wounded desire to restore an imagined past by destroying whatever blocks it.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Agency (the will to act on the world by destroying obstacles) and Status (iconographic in-group coding), but the load-bearing payload is affective: governing through 'dream logic' that metabolizes a wounded longing for a lost past. Genuinely cross-cutting.
signals.novelty_note: Names 'dream logic' as a governing medium — politics conducted through affectively-charged image rather than argument.

signals.title: Directing the Herd
signals.summary: Edward Ongweso Jr. revisits the Lippmann-Dewey debate over whether masses can self-govern, arguing that corporate digital platforms have replaced genuine public discourse with algorithmic management. The result is competing fragmented sub-publics rather than collective deliberation, with AI now threatening what remains of democratic knowledge-sharing.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Primary pull Connection (the collapse of a shared public into fragmented sub-publics is about who we can deliberate and belong with), heavily entangled with Agency (self-governance, collective voice). Borderline unsettled.
signals.novelty_note: Names 'algorithmic management' of the public as the successor to discourse — the public sphere reframed as an administered system, not a conversation.

signals.title: History Has Its Eyes on You: Slam Frank and Musical Theater's Hamilton Bind
signals.summary: Emma Adler examines how Hamilton and its imitators tried to reconcile history with progressive values, and why that formula now reads as flawed—dramatizing historical suffering alongside modern grievance paradoxically trivializes present concerns. She argues satirical works like Slam Frank and Oh, Mary! better capture audience disillusionment by abandoning the pretense that progressive retelling can be gotten 'right.'
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names a new mode of evaluation (satirical abandonment of 'gettable-right' progressive retelling). Touches Status (prestige economy of the progressive-musical formula) and Agency (refusal of a didactic mode), but the felt core is disillusionment and its management.
signals.novelty_note: Names the 'Hamilton bind' and the satirical exit from it — a new evaluative stance that treats earnest progressive retelling as itself the problem.

signals.title: Not Quite Nonsense
signals.summary: Mae Losasso reviews Jennifer Scappettone's Poetry After Barbarism, which frames xenoglossic poetry (writing in 'tongues officially foreign' to the poet) as resistance to fascism and nationalism through linguistic instability. Losasso argues that while Scappettone's call for 'studious unlearning' opens real political possibilities, it risks obscuring the substantial expertise such poetic practice actually demands.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Surfaces a new conceptual frame ('studious unlearning' / xenoglossia as resistance). Primarily Agency (refusal, voice, self-authorship through linguistic destabilization) but brushes Vitality (generative instability) and Connection (language as belonging). Concept is more proposed-by-book than observed.
signals.novelty_note: Names 'studious unlearning' and xenoglossic poetry as a structured practice of resistance — refusal enacted at the level of language itself.

signals.title: The Loneliness of the Competitive Quizzer
signals.summary: Drew Basile argues competitive quizzing offers isolated, often unemployed knowledge workers a pseudo-meritocratic refuge where fact accumulation supplies identity and purpose. Yet the system reinforces the loneliness it promises to cure, an endless arms race masking anxieties about labor-market obsolescence and the futility of knowledge 'the market certainly wouldn't reward.'
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Clean Coping: an emerging refuge-structure for managing the felt weight of labor-market obsolescence, where fact-accumulation supplies borrowed purpose. Touches Status (pseudo-meritocratic ranking) and Connection (the loneliness it fails to cure) as symptoms the structure manages.
signals.novelty_note: Names competitive quizzing as a coping-architecture for knowledge-worker obsolescence — a refuge that re-instantiates the anxiety it promises to relieve.

signals.title: Superhuman Fantasies
signals.summary: Nicholas Low argues Silicon Valley techno-optimists like Marc Andreessen misappropriate Nietzsche's Übermensch by equating superhuman transcendence with technological enhancement and computational speed. Nietzsche, Low contends, envisioned the superhuman as one who affirms finitude and suffering rather than escaping it through technology—so genuine self-overcoming requires renouncing the nihilistic urge to engineer suffering away.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names an emerging conceptual frame: techno-transcendence recast as a nihilistic refusal to bear finitude. Heavily touches Agency (mastery, engineering the world) and Vitality (affirmation of suffering as aliveness), but the diagnostic core is how to relate to mortality and pain.
signals.novelty_note: Reframes Silicon Valley techno-optimism as a coping pathology — enhancement-as-escape from finitude, opposed to suffering-affirming self-overcoming.

signals.title: Why creativity shines out on the edge of things
signals.summary: The essay argues that creativity—biological and cultural—flourishes at edges: the margins of a population, the rim of a landmass, the boundary of viability or orthodoxy. Drawing on island ecology (field mice on St Kilda) and Iain McGilchrist, it treats 'edges' as metaphor and material fact, claiming that fecundity arises precisely where old inhibitions relax and new challenges press.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names a conceptual frame — the 'edge' as the site of generativity — leaning Vitality (fecundity, force, relaxing of inhibition as a source of aliveness) but also Agency (self-authorship at the margin of orthodoxy). Somewhat perennial/metaphorical, so low confidence.
signals.novelty_note: Names the 'edge' (ecological and cultural) as the structural locus of creativity — fecundity as a property of margins, not centers.

signals.title: How does the deep Earth see humanity?
signals.summary: The essay argues that from the planet's perspective humans are a 'shallow' species, yet our subsurface influence is now staggering—human-caused fluid flux from oil, gas, and mining exceeds natural deep groundwater flow below 500 metres. It reframes the Anthropocene debate around how deep human influence reaches (into the upper mantle, the carbon shift from lithosphere to atmosphere) rather than merely when it began.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: A new conceptual frame (Anthropocene re-axed from 'when' to 'how deep') that is pre-categorical relative to felt human needs. Distantly touches Coping (scale reframing climate guilt) and Agency (magnitude of human action), but doesn't resolve into a need-structure.
signals.novelty_note: Reframes the Anthropocene around depth rather than date — human influence measured by how far into the Earth it reaches, not when it began.

signals.title: Why we need to think again about ecosystem failure
signals.summary: Written by a philosopher-ecologist, the essay argues that calling an ecosystem 'failed' (an algal bloom, coral bleaching) imports human duties, norms, and objectives that are external to the ecosystem itself. It bridges philosophical debates over the concept of 'function' with ecologists' unreflective use of the same word, questioning whether ecosystems can fail in any sense independent of human concern.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Clears the gate as a new mode of evaluation (interrogating whether 'failure' is coherent applied to non-human systems). Genuinely pre-categorical with respect to human need-substrates — it questions the projection of human norms onto nature.
signals.novelty_note: Names the move of stripping human-imported norms from ecological judgment — questioning whether 'failure' applies to a system independent of human concern.

signals.title: Kony 2012 Forever
signals.summary: Andrew Lee argues Kony 2012 pioneered a propaganda model that stripped political complexity from Uganda's conflict—obscuring Western-backed government abuses while casting the LRA as pure evil requiring military intervention. He contends this template of decontextualized atrocity footage, built to manufacture demand for military action, has become a blueprint shaping how Western audiences consume later conflicts.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names a persistent structural form (the 'Kony 2012' template for consuming conflict via decontextualized atrocity footage). Touches Agency (manufactured demand for intervention) and Connection (mediated moral spectatorship), but the load-bearing function is how publics metabolize distant atrocity. Cross-cutting.
signals.novelty_note: Names the 'Kony 2012' template as a durable media blueprint — decontextualized atrocity engineered to manufacture the feeling of righteous demand.

signals.title: Will gossip save digital media?
signals.summary: As Google's AI search guts SEO-driven traffic, Kate Lindsay argues digital media must pivot to content AI can't replicate. She suggests gossip and personality-driven journalism may become the differentiator that keeps outlets alive in the post-search landscape.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names an emerging structural form (gossip/personality as the AI-proof differentiator for media). Primary pull Status (gossip is location in social space, in-group knowledge, distinction), with strong Connection adjacency (gossip as binding ritual). Touches both without fully resolving.
signals.novelty_note: Names gossip and personality as the post-AI-search survival strategy for media — human social knowledge reframed as the un-automatable product.

signals.title: I let Apple AI answer all my texts
signals.summary: Lindsay documents an experiment using Apple's AI-suggested replies to fix her habit of leaving texts unanswered. The feature instead produced vague, sometimes rude messages that alienated her contacts—an essay on how automating intimacy degrades rather than smooths human connection.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Clean Connection: directly about intimacy and how outsourcing the labor of response corrodes the bond it was meant to maintain. Touches Coping (the original motive was managing reply-anxiety) and Agency (delegating one's voice), but the substrate at stake is the relationship.
signals.novelty_note: Names 'automated intimacy' as a degrading force — the emerging behavioral pattern of delegating relational labor to AI and the relational cost it incurs.

signals.title: The social contract around phones is broken
signals.summary: Using Alamo Drafthouse's move to phone-based ordering during films as a case, Lindsay argues phone etiquette's shared social contract has collapsed. People increasingly treat others as 'NPCs' and public spaces as extensions of their personal digital worlds rather than shared rooms requiring mutual consideration.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Names an emerging structure of feeling — the 'NPC-ification' of strangers and the dissolution of shared public space into private digital worlds. Primary Connection (mutual recognition, the social contract of co-presence). Touches Agency (treating surroundings as a personal world) and Coping (retreat into a controllable bubble).
signals.novelty_note: Names 'NPC'-treatment of strangers and the collapse of co-presence — public space recast as an extension of one's private digital world.

signals.title: Unemployment and burnout issues spotlighted by Arts University Plymouth students
signals.summary: Dezeen School Shows feature on Arts University Plymouth graduate work, including a graphic/communication project about entering the creative industries amid self-employment, economic uncertainty and AI-generated imagery, plus a toolkit for creatives experiencing burnout. Frames precarity and AI anxiety as the defining conditions for emerging designers.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Agency (authoring a viable career under precarity) and Status (anxiety about position in a collapsing hierarchy), but the deliverable is a burnout toolkit — a structure to make a felt weight bearable.
signals.novelty_note: Design students treating their OWN economic precarity and AI-displacement anxiety as the design brief, rather than an external client problem.

signals.title: Time management pebble among industrial design projects from the University of Illinois Chicago
signals.summary: UIC industrial design students present assistive objects for neurodivergent people, led by 'Pebs' — a system of small glowing objects supporting awareness of time, task initiation and transitions for people who struggle with time perception and sustained focus. Signals a shift toward neurodivergence-centered, calm-tech product design.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Agency (the object restores task-initiation and self-direction) but the primary register is assistive design absorbing the felt overwhelm of time-blindness — making daily life bearable.
signals.novelty_note: Neurodivergent time-perception treated as a designable sensory environment (glowing ambient objects) rather than a productivity-app problem.

signals.title: Flood-management infrastructure among projects from the School of Visual Arts
signals.summary: SVA student work including 'ReLoop,' a public food-rescue hub that intercepts surplus and cosmetically imperfect produce from farmers and redirects it to food-insecure communities while making the logistics visible. Emphasis on civic infrastructure and making invisible systems legible.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Connection (feeding food-insecure communities) and Coping (food security as relief), but the structural move is civic/infrastructural intervention that makes a hidden system legible and actionable — acting on the world.
signals.novelty_note: Designing the VISIBILITY of logistics as the product — legibility of a supply chain as a civic act, not just the redistribution itself.

signals.title: Centre for dance and wellbeing among projects from IE University
signals.summary: IE University project 'El Ritmo de Casa Común' reimagines luxury as a shared condition inside Nave 15 at Matadero Madrid, organizing a three-level domestic system (thermal pools and kitchen, wooden rehearsal platforms, insulated housing) where circulation turns movement into spatial choreography. Reframes luxury from individual consumption to communal access supporting bodily practice.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Genuinely cross-cutting: redefines luxury (Status) as communal access (Connection) organized around bodily movement and pleasure (Vitality). The collision of Status and its negation makes it pre-categorical.
signals.novelty_note: Luxury redefined as a shared, movement-based spatial condition rather than private consumption — status logic inverted into communal vitality.

signals.title: Arching motion-informed amphitheatre among projects from University of Dundee
signals.summary: University of Dundee project 'Cambré' reimagines the amphitheatre as a grid of differently shaped arches over a sunken stage in Dundee Botanic Gardens, with form derived from dance and motion. Part of a society-driven student cohort applying choreographic logic to public architecture.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Connection (the amphitheatre as communal form) but the generative logic is choreographic — bodily movement translated into built form — so the destination is felt aliveness and movement.
signals.novelty_note: Architectural form derived from dance/motion rather than program or structure — choreography as a generative design grammar.

signals.title: Proposal for sustainable agriculture factory among projects from UWE Bristol
signals.summary: MArch student Danni Payne (tutors Matthew Hynam, Piers Taylor, Michael Lewis) proposes a 2050 agriculture factory built from shaggy thatch, exposed timber and manure plaster, returning industrial production to the high street with soil-research labs and exhibition galleries above. Argues for an 'honest,' materially-expressive approach to re-localized agriculture.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Vitality (raw, expressive materials — thatch, manure plaster) and Coping (ecological anxiety), but the core gesture is an infrastructural intervention re-authoring where and how production happens.
signals.novelty_note: Industrial agriculture returned to the high street as a visible, materially 'honest' civic building — productive infrastructure as public spectacle.

signals.title: Zero-waste textiles project among work featured at New Designers 2026
signals.summary: New Designers 2026 preview led by 'Interwoven: Reclaiming the Domestic Fibre,' a textiles project using found, deadstock and second-hand yarn via a zero-waste construction process of laser-cutting and reassembling knitted panels. Continues the material-circularity and domestic-craft revival thread among UK graduates.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Cross-cutting between Coping (circularity as a response to ecological felt weight), Agency (refusal of waste-based production), and Connection (reclaiming the domestic/craft register). No single need dominates; ecological-consolation edges it toward Coping but low confidence.
signals.novelty_note: Zero-waste reframed as reconstruction (laser-cut and reassemble existing knits) rather than virgin sustainable sourcing — repair-logic over supply-logic.

signals.title: Homeware objects that support ADHD individuals among work at New Designers 2026
signals.summary: New Designers 2026 feature on homeware objects designed to support people with ADHD in daily domestic routines. Reinforces a 2026 grad-cohort pattern of neurodivergence-informed product and homeware design.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Agency (objects that help users execute daily routines) but the primary register is assistive design absorbing the overwhelm of ADHD daily life. Part of a clear cohort-level pattern with the UIC 'Pebs' signal.
signals.novelty_note: Neurodivergence-support migrating from clinical/productivity tools into ordinary domestic homeware — the home itself as an assistive system.

signals.title: Rehab centre among projects from Florence Institute of Design International
signals.summary: Florence Institute of Design International interior design students present work led by a rehabilitation centre for young people struggling with addiction. Signals interior-design students addressing youth mental health and recovery environments.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Connection (recovery as communal/relational) but the destination is a refuge environment for managing addiction, grief and youth mental-health weight — consolation and recovery.
signals.novelty_note: Interior design students designing recovery/refuge environments for youth addiction — mental-health spatial design entering the grad-show mainstream.

signals.title: Proposal for beer factory museum among projects from the University of Bath
signals.summary: University of Bath architecture students present work led by a proposal for a beer factory museum, part of a broader cohort interest in productive/industrial heritage buildings as cultural and public destinations.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Thin summary, no clear human need foregrounded. Part of an emerging movement (productive/industrial heritage as public culture) shared with the UWE agriculture-factory signal, but sits between Status (heritage-as-distinction), Vitality (productive spectacle) and Connection (public destination).
signals.novelty_note: Cohort-level turn toward turning sites of production (breweries, factories) into public cultural destinations — the factory as museum.

signals.title: Sculptural wooden play apparatus among projects from the Architectural Association
signals.summary: AA School (London) student work led by a sculptural timber play apparatus, shown ahead of the school's end-of-year Projects Review. Reflects a play/childhood-spatial-experience strand in 2026 architecture grad work.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Touches Connection (play as shared/social) but the central register is embodied play, movement and sensory aliveness. Part of a play/childhood-spatial strand in 2026 architecture.
signals.novelty_note: Play apparatus treated as sculptural/architectural research object rather than playground equipment — childhood movement as a serious design subject.

signals.title: Ecological research centre with tree-inspired design among projects from Politecnico di Torino and University of Belgrade
signals.summary: Joint Politecnico di Torino / University of Belgrade architecture projects led by an ecological research centre whose form is informed by the 'growth rings' of trees; the showcase also includes a science museum with a timber thatched roof and a school extension with library and playground. Biomorphic and timber-forward ecological architecture from emerging students.
signals.cross_substrate_notes: Cross-cutting: biomorphic/ecological form sits between Coping (ecological-anxiety consolation, refuge in nature-derived form), Agency (ecological research as intervention) and Vitality (living, growth-derived form). Summary is aesthetic-led, low confidence.
signals.novelty_note: Architectural form derived from biological growth logic (tree growth rings) coupled with timber-forward construction — biomimicry as the default ecological-architecture grammar for emerging students.
